==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|selfe|silf|silfe||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:self|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|salve}}, {{m|enm|self}}, {{m|enm|silf}}, from {{inh|en|ang|self}}, {{m|ang|seolf}}, {{m|ang|sylf}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*selbaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*selbʰ-|t=one's own}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognates with {{cog|stq|sälven}}, {{m|stq|säärm}}, {{m|stq|sääuwen|t=oneself}}, {{cog|fy|sels|t=oneself}}, {{cog|bar|söbe|t=identical, same}}, {{m|bar|söber|t=self}}, {{cog|nl|zelf|t=myself, oneself}}, {{cog|de|selber|t=self}}, {{m|de|selbst|t=by oneself}}, {{cog|lb|selwer|t=self}}, {{cog|yi|זעלב|t=same}}, {{cog|da|selv|t=self}}, {{cog|ovd|siuov|t=self}}, {{cog|fo|sjálvur|t=self}}, {{cog|is|sjálfur|t=self}}, {{cog|nb|selv}}, {{cog|nn|sjølv}}, {{cog|sv|själv|t=self}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌹𐌻𐌱𐌰|t=self}}. {{col-bottom}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈsɛlf/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈsɛf/|a=Southern US,AAVE,dated|ref={{R:Hall PGSMS|3|2|88}}}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈsɛl/|a=Northumbria}} * {{audio|en|en-us-self.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛlf|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|self}} ===Pronoun=== {{en-pron|plural|selves}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|_|or|_|rare|}} [[himself|Himself]], [[herself]], [[itself]], [[themself]], [[themselves]]; that specific (person mentioned). #: {{ux|en|This argument was put forward by the defendant '''self'''.}} # {{lb|en|commercial|_|or|_|humorous}} [[myself|Myself]], [[oneself]]. #: {{ux|en|I made out a cheque, payable to '''self''', which cheered me up somewhat.}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|selves|s}} # One individual's [[personality]], [[character]], [[demeanor]], or [[disposition]]. #: {{ux|en|She remained her usual cheerful '''self''' despite recent setbacks}} #* '''2003''', {{w|Roy_Porter|Roy Porter}}, ''Flesh in the Age of Reason'', Ch.1, at p.7: #*: {{w|John Locke}} argued that the mind is not like a furnished flat, prestocked before occupation with innate ideas, but like a home put together piecemeal from mental acquisitions picked up bit by bit. The '''self''' is thus the bit-by-bit product of experience and education: we are what we become - or, in {{w|William Wordsworth|Wordworth's}} later phrase, the child is the father of the man. Particular parents, surroundings and stimuli produce individuated selves. Identity is thus unique because contingent, the cumulative product of ceaseless occurrences. # The [[subject]] of one's own [[experience]] of [[phenomenon|phenomena]]: perception, emotions, thoughts. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|II|ix|text={{smallcaps|Portia}}:
To these injunctions every one doth swear
That comes to hazard for my worthless '''self'''.}} #* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|I|0056 |passage=Thanks to that penny he had just spent so recklessly [on a newspaper] he would pass a happy hour, taken, for once, out of his anxious, despondent, miserable '''self'''. It irritated him shrewdly to know that these moments of respite from carking care would not be shared with his poor wife, with careworn, troubled Ellen.}} # An individual [[person]] as the object of the person's own [[reflective]] [[consciousness]] (plural [[selves]]). #* {{RQ:Hamilton Metaphysics and Logic|chapter=Lecture IX|text=The '''self''', the I, is recognized in every act of intelligence as the subject to which that act belongs. It is I that perceive, I that imagine, I that remember, I that attend, I that compare, I that feel, I that will, I that am conscious.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=16|passage=The preposterous altruism too!{{...}}Resist not evil. It is an insane immolation of '''self'''—as bad intrinsically as fakirs stabbing themselves or anchorites warping their spines in caves scarcely large enough for a fair-sized dog.}} # Self-interest or personal advantage. # {{lb|en|botany}} A seedling produced by self-pollination (plural {{m|en|selfs}}). # {{lb|en|botany}} A [[flower]] having its colour [[uniform]] as opposed to [[variegated]]. #
